PRIMARY CARE NOTE   Date: 2026-05-22
61M, ambulatory visit for an annual check-up.

S:
Patient presents for a routine check-up. He reports feeling well overall and staying active with regular walking and weekend yard work. He takes his blood pressure medication each morning and checks home readings twice a week. Patient denies depression. No shortness of breath. Appetite is good, weight stable. He works part time as a hardware store clerk and enjoys time with his grandchildren. Sleep is about 7 hours most nights. Lives with his spouse, with good support at home. Never smoker, rare alcohol. No new concerns today.

O:
BP 126/78, HR 68, RR 14, Temp 98.3 F, SpO2 98% on room air. Weight 184 lb, BMI 26.
General: well appearing, in no distress.
HEENT: normal.
Neck: no lymphadenopathy, no thyromegaly.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur, no gallop.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Abdomen: soft, nontender, no organomegaly.
Extremities: no edema, pulses intact.
Labs (prior week): basic metabolic panel normal, lipid panel within goal, A1c 5.5%.
PHQ-2 score 0.

A/P:
1. Essential hypertension, well controlled on current regimen. Continue lisinopril 10 mg daily. Home readings reviewed, averaging 124/78. Repeat basic metabolic panel in 12 months.
2. Health maintenance: colorectal screening up to date. Shingles vaccine discussed; patient will schedule. Influenza vaccine given today. Encouraged continued walking and adding light strength exercises twice weekly.
3. Lifestyle: reviewed balanced meals and hydration. Reinforced regular physical activity and adequate sleep.

Return in 12 months for the next wellness visit, sooner as needed.
